label.description: The list's accessible name, forwarded as aria-label. REQUIRED unless labelledby names a visible heading: listbox takes its name from a label rather than from its rows, so an unnamed one is announced as "listbox" and nothing else. Nothing lints it — a bound role makes the naming rules stand down — so the element's own test is what holds it.

labelledby.description: Forwarded as aria-labelledby, naming the element that already says what this list is.

active.description: The ID of the row the caret is on; the empty string when none is. THIS IS THE ONE STRING A CONSUMER WRITES: the same id its owning field points aria-activedescendant at, so the field and the row are told the same thing once instead of the question being re-decided per row. The sidecar turns it into each row's selected and scrolls the new one back into view.

onMount.description: Keeps every row's selected in step with active for as long as the element lives, and scrolls the active row into view. Both are things a document body cannot say: the flag lives on a foreign element, and scrolling is a measurement.

style.$description: There is deliberately NO tabindex here, and no rule that draws a focus ring: the element never takes DOM focus. One of its two owners is a field that must keep the caret, and the other is nothing at all — a panel filtering for a caret in another realm. A listbox that is operated from somewhere else is exactly the shape ARIA's aria-activedescendant exists for.

& [part=\"group-heading\"].$description: A furniture part a CONSUMER writes, styled from here because this is the definition that owns the box it sits in (ui.md 3.1). A grouped list is a role="group" wrapper holding a heading and its rows — the formula palette's shape — and in a light DOM the container's own rule reaches it without a class, which is the whole point of the cascade being one.

& [part=\"empty\"].$description: The other furniture part: the sentence a consumer draws when its own filter matched nothing. What that sentence SAYS belongs to the surface — "No matches", "Nothing here yet", a hint about the mode — so the element draws it and never writes it.
